payload.title: How To Activate Flow State, According To Science
payload.summary: The Neuroscience of Flow, Peak Performance, Psychedelics, Trauma, Intuition & Consciousness with Steven Kotler Host Dave Asprey sits down with Steven Kotler, New York Times bestselling author and leading researcher in the neuroscience of flow, to explore how altered states of consciousness influence peak performance, mental health, creativity, intuition, and our perception of reality. Steven Kotler is a bestselling author of 17 books, including The Art of Impossible and We Are as Gods, and the founder of the Flow Research Collective. For decades, he has studied the neurobiology of peak performance, working with elite athletes, military personnel, and high-performing professionals to understand how people can reliably access flow states. Dave and Steven begin by exploring the neuroscience of flow and why it may be one of the most powerful altered states available without drugs. Steven explains how dopamine, norepinephrine, serotonin, anandamide, and endorphins contribute to the flow experience, why his research suggests caffeine can increase flow susceptibility, and how chasing the neurochemical high of peak performance can become dangerous. Finally, Steven reveals new research investigating the neurological connections between flow, intuition, synchronicity, and purpose. He discusses emerging theories of consciousness, the role of information processing in subjective experience, and how artificial intelligence may change the future of human performance. You'll Learn: * How…

payload.title: Morning Routine Expert: 6 Minutes Every Morning Changes Your Whole Day
payload.summary: The Miracle Morning, Visualization, Affirmations, Meditation, Morning Routines, Productivity & the Psychology of Success with Hal Elrod Host Dave Asprey sits down with Hal Elrod, bestselling author of The Miracle Morning and personal development expert, to explore morning routines, visualization, affirmations, meditation, productivity, circadian rhythms, habit formation, and the psychology of success. Hal Elrod is the creator of The Miracle Morning, a bestselling book and personal development method that has helped millions improve their daily habits. After surviving a devastating car accident at age 20 and later battling life-threatening cancer, Hal developed a philosophy centered on resilience, personal responsibility, and consistent daily practices. Dave and Hal challenge the idea that success requires waking up at 5 AM. They discuss chronotypes, circadian biology, and why morning routines should work with your natural sleep patterns. Hal introduces his six-part SAVERS framework, explaining how meditation, affirmations, visualization, exercise, reading, and journaling can transform your morning in as little as six minutes. They explore how smartphones disrupt attention, why visualization works best when paired with mental rehearsal, and how these techniques can help overcome procrastination. Hal shares how he used visualization to train for a 52-mile ultramarathon, while Dave discusses advanced meditation, neurofeedback, and the role of emotional states in mental…

payload.title: CJC-1295 Explained: Does It Really Increase Growth Hormone?
payload.summary: Does CJC-1295 really increase growth hormone? 🧬 CJC-1295 is often discussed alongside growth hormone, muscle growth, fat loss, recovery, and anti-aging—but CJC-1295 is not growth hormone. It's a synthetic analog of growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH) designed to stimulate the pituitary gland, which can increase the body's own release of growth hormone (GH) and raise IGF-1 levels. Early human research involving the long-acting DAC form of CJC-1295 found that a single dose produced sustained increases in average growth hormone and IGF-1 levels. But there's an important distinction: Increasing GH and IGF-1 does NOT automatically prove that CJC-1295 builds muscle, burns fat, improves longevity, or reverses aging. Changing a biomarker and demonstrating a meaningful clinical benefit are two very different things. In this Peptide A to Z Short, we break down what CJC-1295 actually does, how the pituitary → GH → IGF-1 pathway works, and why it's important to separate human research from claims made online. 🧬 Follow Peptide A to Z for evidence-based coverage of peptides, clinical trials, longevity science, GLP-1 research, and emerging compounds. payload.title: CJC-1295 Explained: Does It Really Increase Growth Hormone?
payload.summary: Does CJC-1295 really increase growth hormone? 🧬 CJC-1295 is often discussed alongside growth hormone, muscle growth, fat loss, recovery, and anti-aging—but CJC-1295 is not growth hormone. It's a synthetic analog of growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH) designed to stimulate the pituitary gland, which can increase the body's own release of growth hormone (GH) and raise IGF-1 levels. Early human research involving the long-acting DAC form of CJC-1295 found that a single dose produced sustained increases in average growth hormone and IGF-1 levels. But there's an important distinction: Increasing GH and IGF-1 does NOT automatically prove that CJC-1295 builds muscle, burns fat, improves longevity, or reverses aging. Changing a biomarker and demonstrating a meaningful clinical benefit are two very different things. In this Peptide A to Z Short, we break down what CJC-1295 actually does, how the pituitary → GH → IGF-1 pathway works, and why it's important to separate human research from claims made online. 🧬 Follow Peptide A to Z for evidence-based coverage of peptides, clinical trials, longevity science, GLP-1 research, and emerging compounds. It's a synthetic analog of growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH) designed to stimulate the pituitary gland, which can increase the body's own release of growth hormone (GH) and raise IGF-1 levels. Early human research involving the long-acting DAC form of CJC-1295 found that a single dose produced sustained increases in average growth hormone and IGF-1 levels. But there's an important distinction: Increasing GH and IGF-1 does NOT automatically prove that CJC-1295 builds muscle, burns fat, improves longevity, or reverses aging. Changing a biomarker and demonstrating a meaningful clinical benefit are two very different things. payload.title: CJC-1295 Explained: Does It Really Increase Growth Hormone?
payload.summary: Does CJC-1295 really increase growth hormone? 🧬 CJC-1295 is often discussed alongside growth hormone, muscle growth, fat loss, recovery, and anti-aging—but CJC-1295 is not growth hormone. It's a synthetic analog of growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH) designed to stimulate the pituitary gland, which can increase the body's own release of growth hormone (GH) and raise IGF-1 levels. Early human research involving the long-acting DAC form of CJC-1295 found that a single dose produced sustained increases in average growth hormone and IGF-1 levels. But there's an important distinction: Increasing GH and IGF-1 does NOT automatically prove that CJC-1295 builds muscle, burns fat, improves longevity, or reverses aging. Changing a biomarker and demonstrating a meaningful clinical benefit are two very different things. In this Peptide A to Z Short, we break down what CJC-1295 actually does, how the pituitary → GH → IGF-1 pathway works, and why it's important to separate human research from claims made online. 🧬 Follow Peptide A to Z for evidence-based coverage of peptides, clinical trials, longevity science, GLP-1 research, and emerging compounds. payload.title: Sleep Doctor REVEALS: Do This To Turn On Your Sleep Switch Tonight
payload.summary: Sleep Anxiety, Insomnia, Circadian Rhythms, Chronotypes, Sleep Trackers & How to Sleep Better with Dr. Michael Breus Host Dave Asprey sits down with Dr. Michael Breus, clinical psychologist, sleep specialist, and internationally recognized sleep expert known as The Sleep Doctor, to explore insomnia, sleep anxiety, circadian rhythms, chronotypes, nighttime awakenings, temperature regulation, sleep medications, wearable sleep trackers, and the science of improving sleep quality. The conversation challenges conventional thinking about sleep, including whether everyone needs eight hours, why trying harder to fall asleep can make insomnia worse, and how the body's internal clock influences energy, productivity, and recovery. Dr. Breus explains why he believes fear and anxiety contribute to a substantial proportion of sleep problems. He describes how worrying about falling asleep, waking up at 3 a.m., or feeling exhausted the next day can create a cycle of stress that makes restful sleep increasingly difficult. Dave and Michael explore how cognitive behavioral therapy, emotional regulation, and changing your relationship with sleep may help break that cycle without relying exclusively on medication. The conversation explores why sleeping pills may fail to address the underlying causes of chronic insomnia, how nighttime awakenings can trigger negative thinking, and why the fear of being tired may sometimes become more disruptive than the tiredness itself. Dave shares his experience…

payload.title: CJC-1295 Explained: Does It Really Increase Growth Hormone?
payload.summary: Does CJC-1295 really increase growth hormone? 🧬 CJC-1295 is often discussed alongside growth hormone, muscle growth, fat loss, recovery, and anti-aging—but CJC-1295 is not growth hormone. It's a synthetic analog of growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH) designed to stimulate the pituitary gland, which can increase the body's own release of growth hormone (GH) and raise IGF-1 levels. Early human research involving the long-acting DAC form of CJC-1295 found that a single dose produced sustained increases in average growth hormone and IGF-1 levels. But there's an important distinction: Increasing GH and IGF-1 does NOT automatically prove that CJC-1295 builds muscle, burns fat, improves longevity, or reverses aging. Changing a biomarker and demonstrating a meaningful clinical benefit are two very different things. payload.title: GLP-1 Once a Month?! New VK2735 Results Could Change Weight Loss
payload.summary: What if you didn't have to take a GLP-1 every week — but only once a month? New clinical trial results for VK2735, an experimental GLP-1/GIP drug from Viking Therapeutics, suggest that less-frequent dosing could eventually play a role in maintaining weight loss. In the study, participants first received weekly VK2735 and lost approximately 16% to 19% of their body weight after 21 weeks. Researchers then tested less-frequent maintenance dosing. The results were fascinating: 💉 Every-other-week dosing maintained up to 97% of previous weight loss 📅 Once-monthly dosing maintained up to 90% ⚖️ Participants switched to placebo maintained about 61% 📉 A small weekly-treatment group reached an average 21.7% weight loss after 33 weeks But there's an important distinction: this does not mean people started with a once-a-month injection and lost 20% of their body weight. Participants first lost weight using weekly VK2735. Researchers then tested whether less-frequent dosing could help maintain those results. That raises a much bigger question for the future of GLP-1 treatment: Could people eventually lose weight with weekly injections, then transition to one injection a month for maintenance? In this video, we break down how VK2735 works, GLP-1 + GIP signaling, the new maintenance data, side effects, limitations of the study, and why the next generation of obesity drugs may compete not only on how much weight people lose — but how rarely they need to take the medication. payload.title: CJC-1295 Explained: Does It Really Increase Growth Hormone?
payload.summary: Does CJC-1295 really increase growth hormone? 🧬 CJC-1295 is often discussed alongside growth hormone, muscle growth, fat loss, recovery, and anti-aging—but CJC-1295 is not growth hormone. It's a synthetic analog of growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH) designed to stimulate the pituitary gland, which can increase the body's own release of growth hormone (GH) and raise IGF-1 levels. Early human research involving the long-acting DAC form of CJC-1295 found that a single dose produced sustained increases in average growth hormone and IGF-1 levels. But there's an important distinction: Increasing GH and IGF-1 does NOT automatically prove that CJC-1295 builds muscle, burns fat, improves longevity, or reverses aging. Changing a biomarker and demonstrating a meaningful clinical benefit are two very different things. In this Peptide A to Z Short, we break down what CJC-1295 actually does, how the pituitary → GH → IGF-1 pathway works, and why it's important to separate human research from claims made online. 🧬 Follow Peptide A to Z for evidence-based coverage of peptides, clinical trials, longevity science, GLP-1 research, and emerging compounds. Peptide science without the hype. ⚠️ Educational and informational purposes only. Not medical advice. Research shows that people taking GLP-1 medications can lose measurable amounts of lean body mass along with fat. payload.title: GLP-1 Once a Month?! New VK2735 Results Could Change Weight Loss
payload.summary: What if you didn't have to take a GLP-1 every week — but only once a month? New clinical trial results for VK2735, an experimental GLP-1/GIP drug from Viking Therapeutics, suggest that less-frequent dosing could eventually play a role in maintaining weight loss. In the study, participants first received weekly VK2735 and lost approximately 16% to 19% of their body weight after 21 weeks. Researchers then tested less-frequent maintenance dosing. The results were fascinating: 💉 Every-other-week dosing maintained up to 97% of previous weight loss 📅 Once-monthly dosing maintained up to 90% ⚖️ Participants switched to placebo maintained about 61% 📉 A small weekly-treatment group reached an average 21.7% weight loss after 33 weeks But there's an important distinction: this does not mean people started with a once-a-month injection and lost 20% of their body weight. Participants first lost weight using weekly VK2735. Researchers then tested whether less-frequent dosing could help maintain those results. That raises a much bigger question for the future of GLP-1 treatment: Could people eventually lose weight with weekly injections, then transition to one injection a month for maintenance? In this video, we break down how VK2735 works, GLP-1 + GIP signaling, the new maintenance data, side effects, limitations of the study, and why the next generation of obesity drugs may compete not only on how much weight people lose — but how rarely they need to take the medication. payload.title: CJC-1295 Explained: Does It Really Increase Growth Hormone?
payload.summary: Does CJC-1295 really increase growth hormone? 🧬 CJC-1295 is often discussed alongside growth hormone, muscle growth, fat loss, recovery, and anti-aging—but CJC-1295 is not growth hormone. It's a synthetic analog of growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH) designed to stimulate the pituitary gland, which can increase the body's own release of growth hormone (GH) and raise IGF-1 levels. Early human research involving the long-acting DAC form of CJC-1295 found that a single dose produced sustained increases in average growth hormone and IGF-1 levels. But there's an important distinction: Increasing GH and IGF-1 does NOT automatically prove that CJC-1295 builds muscle, burns fat, improves longevity, or reverses aging. Changing a biomarker and demonstrating a meaningful clinical benefit are two very different things. In this Peptide A to Z Short, we break down what CJC-1295 actually does, how the pituitary → GH → IGF-1 pathway works, and why it's important to separate human research from claims made online. 🧬 Follow Peptide A to Z for evidence-based coverage of peptides, clinical trials, longevity science, GLP-1 research, and emerging compounds. payload.title: CJC-1295 Explained: Does It Really Increase Growth Hormone?
payload.summary: Does CJC-1295 really increase growth hormone? 🧬 CJC-1295 is often discussed alongside growth hormone, muscle growth, fat loss, recovery, and anti-aging—but CJC-1295 is not growth hormone. It's a synthetic analog of growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH) designed to stimulate the pituitary gland, which can increase the body's own release of growth hormone (GH) and raise IGF-1 levels. Early human research involving the long-acting DAC form of CJC-1295 found that a single dose produced sustained increases in average growth hormone and IGF-1 levels. But there's an important distinction: Increasing GH and IGF-1 does NOT automatically prove that CJC-1295 builds muscle, burns fat, improves longevity, or reverses aging. Changing a biomarker and demonstrating a meaningful clinical benefit are two very different things. payload.title: GLP-1 Once a Month?! New VK2735 Results Could Change Weight Loss
payload.summary: What if you didn't have to take a GLP-1 every week — but only once a month? New clinical trial results for VK2735, an experimental GLP-1/GIP drug from Viking Therapeutics, suggest that less-frequent dosing could eventually play a role in maintaining weight loss. In the study, participants first received weekly VK2735 and lost approximately 16% to 19% of their body weight after 21 weeks. Researchers then tested less-frequent maintenance dosing. The results were fascinating: 💉 Every-other-week dosing maintained up to 97% of previous weight loss 📅 Once-monthly dosing maintained up to 90% ⚖️ Participants switched to placebo maintained about 61% 📉 A small weekly-treatment group reached an average 21.7% weight loss after 33 weeks But there's an important distinction: this does not mean people started with a once-a-month injection and lost 20% of their body weight. Participants first lost weight using weekly VK2735. Researchers then tested whether less-frequent dosing could help maintain those results. That raises a much bigger question for the future of GLP-1 treatment: Could people eventually lose weight with weekly injections, then transition to one injection a month for maintenance? In this video, we break down how VK2735 works, GLP-1 + GIP signaling, the new maintenance data, side effects, limitations of the study, and why the next generation of obesity drugs may compete not only on how much weight people lose — but how rarely they need to take the medication. payload.title: CJC-1295 Explained: Does It Really Increase Growth Hormone?
payload.summary: Does CJC-1295 really increase growth hormone? 🧬 CJC-1295 is often discussed alongside growth hormone, muscle growth, fat loss, recovery, and anti-aging—but CJC-1295 is not growth hormone. It's a synthetic analog of growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH) designed to stimulate the pituitary gland, which can increase the body's own release of growth hormone (GH) and raise IGF-1 levels. Early human research involving the long-acting DAC form of CJC-1295 found that a single dose produced sustained increases in average growth hormone and IGF-1 levels. But there's an important distinction: Increasing GH and IGF-1 does NOT automatically prove that CJC-1295 builds muscle, burns fat, improves longevity, or reverses aging. Changing a biomarker and demonstrating a meaningful clinical benefit are two very different things. payload.title: GLP-1 Once a Month?! New VK2735 Results Could Change Weight Loss
payload.summary: What if you didn't have to take a GLP-1 every week — but only once a month? New clinical trial results for VK2735, an experimental GLP-1/GIP drug from Viking Therapeutics, suggest that less-frequent dosing could eventually play a role in maintaining weight loss. In the study, participants first received weekly VK2735 and lost approximately 16% to 19% of their body weight after 21 weeks. Researchers then tested less-frequent maintenance dosing. The results were fascinating: 💉 Every-other-week dosing maintained up to 97% of previous weight loss 📅 Once-monthly dosing maintained up to 90% ⚖️ Participants switched to placebo maintained about 61% 📉 A small weekly-treatment group reached an average 21.7% weight loss after 33 weeks But there's an important distinction: this does not mean people started with a once-a-month injection and lost 20% of their body weight. Participants first lost weight using weekly VK2735. Researchers then tested whether less-frequent dosing could help maintain those results. That raises a much bigger question for the future of GLP-1 treatment: Could people eventually lose weight with weekly injections, then transition to one injection a month for maintenance? In this video, we break down how VK2735 works, GLP-1 + GIP signaling, the new maintenance data, side effects, limitations of the study, and why the next generation of obesity drugs may compete not only on how much weight people lose — but how rarely they need to take the medication. payload.title: CJC-1295 Explained: Does It Really Increase Growth Hormone?
payload.summary: Does CJC-1295 really increase growth hormone? 🧬 CJC-1295 is often discussed alongside growth hormone, muscle growth, fat loss, recovery, and anti-aging—but CJC-1295 is not growth hormone. It's a synthetic analog of growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH) designed to stimulate the pituitary gland, which can increase the body's own release of growth hormone (GH) and raise IGF-1 levels. Early human research involving the long-acting DAC form of CJC-1295 found that a single dose produced sustained increases in average growth hormone and IGF-1 levels. But there's an important distinction: Increasing GH and IGF-1 does NOT automatically prove that CJC-1295 builds muscle, burns fat, improves longevity, or reverses aging. Changing a biomarker and demonstrating a meaningful clinical benefit are two very different things. In this Peptide A to Z Short, we break down what CJC-1295 actually does, how the pituitary → GH → IGF-1 pathway works, and why it's important to separate human research from claims made online. 🧬 Follow Peptide A to Z for evidence-based coverage of peptides, clinical trials, longevity science, GLP-1 research, and emerging compounds. Peptide science without the hype. ⚠️ Educational and informational purposes only. Not medical advice. CJC-1295 is not FDA-approved for anti-aging, muscle building, or fat loss. #CJC1295 #Peptides #GrowthHormone #PeptideResearch #IGF1 ⚠️ DISCLAIMER This video is for educational purposes only. Nothing here constitutes medical advice…

payload.title: GLP-1 Once a Month?! New VK2735 Results Could Change Weight Loss
payload.summary: What if you didn't have to take a GLP-1 every week — but only once a month? New clinical trial results for VK2735, an experimental GLP-1/GIP drug from Viking Therapeutics, suggest that less-frequent dosing could eventually play a role in maintaining weight loss. In the study, participants first received weekly VK2735 and lost approximately 16% to 19% of their body weight after 21 weeks. Researchers then tested less-frequent maintenance dosing. The results were fascinating: 💉 Every-other-week dosing maintained up to 97% of previous weight loss 📅 Once-monthly dosing maintained up to 90% ⚖️ Participants switched to placebo maintained about 61% 📉 A small weekly-treatment group reached an average 21.7% weight loss after 33 weeks But there's an important distinction: this does not mean people started with a once-a-month injection and lost 20% of their body weight. Participants first lost weight using weekly VK2735. Researchers then tested whether less-frequent dosing could help maintain those results. That raises a much bigger question for the future of GLP-1 treatment: Could people eventually lose weight with weekly injections, then transition to one injection a month for maintenance? In this video, we break down how VK2735 works, GLP-1 + GIP signaling, the new maintenance data, side effects, limitations of the study, and why the next generation of obesity drugs may compete not only on how much weight people lose — but how rarely they need to take the medication. The path to RonanRx is fairly unconventional. During the pandemic, I built one of the largest mask manufacturing factories in the US. We could make a million masks in a day. We converted raw polypropylene pellets into finished pallets of masks. I had a background in software from my YC W10 company, so we took a software approach to building our factory. We used machine learning and computer vision to optimize production. We also vertically integrated almost everything. It worked. We built an efficient manufacturing operation and grew the business to 50 million dollars in revenue. Then people actually stopped caring about masks. Fair enough. Around the same time, I decided to try and lose the weight I had gained while building the factory. I ate nothing but chicken for six months. While this diet got some results, I plateaued. payload.title: CJC-1295 Explained: Does It Really Increase Growth Hormone?
payload.summary: Does CJC-1295 really increase growth hormone? 🧬 CJC-1295 is often discussed alongside growth hormone, muscle growth, fat loss, recovery, and anti-aging—but CJC-1295 is not growth hormone. It's a synthetic analog of growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH) designed to stimulate the pituitary gland, which can increase the body's own release of growth hormone (GH) and raise IGF-1 levels. Early human research involving the long-acting DAC form of CJC-1295 found that a single dose produced sustained increases in average growth hormone and IGF-1 levels. But there's an important distinction: Increasing GH and IGF-1 does NOT automatically prove that CJC-1295 builds muscle, burns fat, improves longevity, or reverses aging. Changing a biomarker and demonstrating a meaningful clinical benefit are two very different things. In this Peptide A to Z Short, we break down what CJC-1295 actually does, how the pituitary → GH → IGF-1 pathway works, and why it's important to separate human research from claims made online. 🧬 Follow Peptide A to Z for evidence-based coverage of peptides, clinical trials, longevity science, GLP-1 research, and emerging compounds. Peptide science without the hype. ⚠️ Educational and informational purposes only. Not medical advice. payload.title: GLP-1 Once a Month?! New VK2735 Results Could Change Weight Loss
payload.summary: What if you didn't have to take a GLP-1 every week — but only once a month? New clinical trial results for VK2735, an experimental GLP-1/GIP drug from Viking Therapeutics, suggest that less-frequent dosing could eventually play a role in maintaining weight loss. In the study, participants first received weekly VK2735 and lost approximately 16% to 19% of their body weight after 21 weeks. Researchers then tested less-frequent maintenance dosing. The results were fascinating: 💉 Every-other-week dosing maintained up to 97% of previous weight loss 📅 Once-monthly dosing maintained up to 90% ⚖️ Participants switched to placebo maintained about 61% 📉 A small weekly-treatment group reached an average 21.7% weight loss after 33 weeks But there's an important distinction: this does not mean people started with a once-a-month injection and lost 20% of their body weight. Participants first lost weight using weekly VK2735. Researchers then tested whether less-frequent dosing could help maintain those results. That raises a much bigger question for the future of GLP-1 treatment: Could people eventually lose weight with weekly injections, then transition to one injection a month for maintenance? In this video, we break down how VK2735 works, GLP-1 + GIP signaling, the new maintenance data, side effects, limitations of the study, and why the next generation of obesity drugs may compete not only on how much weight people lose — but how rarely they need to take the medication. payload.title: GLP-1 Pills Are Here — Are They Better Than the Shots?
payload.summary: GLP-1 weight-loss pills are officially here. But are they actually better than injections — or do they come with the same risks in a different package? You may have seen Martha Stewart advertising Foundayo, Lilly's new once-daily GLP-1 pill. But Foundayo isn't simply an injectable GLP-1 turned into a tablet. Its active ingredient, orforglipron, is a non-peptide small molecule designed to activate the GLP-1 receptor. And it's not the only option. Wegovy is now available as an oral semaglutide tablet, giving patients another alternative to weekly GLP-1 injections. In this video, Peptide A to Z breaks down: 💊 GLP-1 pills vs. injections 🧬 How oral Wegovy and Foundayo are different ⚖️ The potential advantages and disadvantages of GLP-1 pills 📉 What clinical trials show about weight loss 🍽️ Appetite control and delayed gastric emptying ⚠️ Side effects and important safety considerations 💉 Daily pills vs. weekly injections 🔬 Why orforglipron isn't actually a peptide 📺 What to know about the Martha Stewart Foundayo campaign 🤔 And the big question: Are GLP-1 pills actually better than the shots? One of the most interesting developments is the science itself. Oral Wegovy contains the peptide semaglutide and uses a formulation designed to help it be absorbed orally. Foundayo takes a completely different approach: orforglipron is a small molecule rather than a peptide, but it targets the same GLP-1 receptor. payload.title: CJC-1295 Explained: Does It Really Increase Growth Hormone?
payload.summary: Does CJC-1295 really increase growth hormone? 🧬 CJC-1295 is often discussed alongside growth hormone, muscle growth, fat loss, recovery, and anti-aging—but CJC-1295 is not growth hormone. It's a synthetic analog of growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH) designed to stimulate the pituitary gland, which can increase the body's own release of growth hormone (GH) and raise IGF-1 levels. Early human research involving the long-acting DAC form of CJC-1295 found that a single dose produced sustained increases in average growth hormone and IGF-1 levels. But there's an important distinction: Increasing GH and IGF-1 does NOT automatically prove that CJC-1295 builds muscle, burns fat, improves longevity, or reverses aging. Changing a biomarker and demonstrating a meaningful clinical benefit are two very different things. In this Peptide A to Z Short, we break down what CJC-1295 actually does, how the pituitary → GH → IGF-1 pathway works, and why it's important to separate human research from claims made online. 🧬 Follow Peptide A to Z for evidence-based coverage of peptides, clinical trials, longevity science, GLP-1 research, and emerging compounds. payload.title: GLP-1 Once a Month?! New VK2735 Results Could Change Weight Loss
payload.summary: What if you didn't have to take a GLP-1 every week — but only once a month? New clinical trial results for VK2735, an experimental GLP-1/GIP drug from Viking Therapeutics, suggest that less-frequent dosing could eventually play a role in maintaining weight loss. In the study, participants first received weekly VK2735 and lost approximately 16% to 19% of their body weight after 21 weeks. Researchers then tested less-frequent maintenance dosing. The results were fascinating: 💉 Every-other-week dosing maintained up to 97% of previous weight loss 📅 Once-monthly dosing maintained up to 90% ⚖️ Participants switched to placebo maintained about 61% 📉 A small weekly-treatment group reached an average 21.7% weight loss after 33 weeks But there's an important distinction: this does not mean people started with a once-a-month injection and lost 20% of their body weight. Participants first lost weight using weekly VK2735. Researchers then tested whether less-frequent dosing could help maintain those results. That raises a much bigger question for the future of GLP-1 treatment: Could people eventually lose weight with weekly injections, then transition to one injection a month for maintenance? In this video, we break down how VK2735 works, GLP-1 + GIP signaling, the new maintenance data, side effects, limitations of the study, and why the next generation of obesity drugs may compete not only on how much weight people lose — but how rarely they need to take the medication. payload.title: CJC-1295 Explained: Does It Really Increase Growth Hormone?
payload.summary: Does CJC-1295 really increase growth hormone? 🧬 CJC-1295 is often discussed alongside growth hormone, muscle growth, fat loss, recovery, and anti-aging—but CJC-1295 is not growth hormone. It's a synthetic analog of growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH) designed to stimulate the pituitary gland, which can increase the body's own release of growth hormone (GH) and raise IGF-1 levels. Early human research involving the long-acting DAC form of CJC-1295 found that a single dose produced sustained increases in average growth hormone and IGF-1 levels. But there's an important distinction: Increasing GH and IGF-1 does NOT automatically prove that CJC-1295 builds muscle, burns fat, improves longevity, or reverses aging. Changing a biomarker and demonstrating a meaningful clinical benefit are two very different things. In this Peptide A to Z Short, we break down what CJC-1295 actually does, how the pituitary → GH → IGF-1 pathway works, and why it's important to separate human research from claims made online. 🧬 Follow Peptide A to Z for evidence-based coverage of peptides, clinical trials, longevity science, GLP-1 research, and emerging compounds. Peptide science without the hype. ⚠️ Educational and informational purposes only. Not medical advice. payload.title: GLP-1 Once a Month?! New VK2735 Results Could Change Weight Loss
payload.summary: What if you didn't have to take a GLP-1 every week — but only once a month? New clinical trial results for VK2735, an experimental GLP-1/GIP drug from Viking Therapeutics, suggest that less-frequent dosing could eventually play a role in maintaining weight loss. In the study, participants first received weekly VK2735 and lost approximately 16% to 19% of their body weight after 21 weeks. Researchers then tested less-frequent maintenance dosing. The results were fascinating: 💉 Every-other-week dosing maintained up to 97% of previous weight loss 📅 Once-monthly dosing maintained up to 90% ⚖️ Participants switched to placebo maintained about 61% 📉 A small weekly-treatment group reached an average 21.7% weight loss after 33 weeks But there's an important distinction: this does not mean people started with a once-a-month injection and lost 20% of their body weight. Participants first lost weight using weekly VK2735. Researchers then tested whether less-frequent dosing could help maintain those results. That raises a much bigger question for the future of GLP-1 treatment: Could people eventually lose weight with weekly injections, then transition to one injection a month for maintenance? In this video, we break down how VK2735 works, GLP-1 + GIP signaling, the new maintenance data, side effects, limitations of the study, and why the next generation of obesity drugs may compete not only on how much weight people lose — but how rarely they need to take the medication. payload.title: GLP-1 Pills Are Here — Are They Better Than the Shots?
payload.summary: GLP-1 weight-loss pills are officially here. But are they actually better than injections — or do they come with the same risks in a different package? You may have seen Martha Stewart advertising Foundayo, Lilly's new once-daily GLP-1 pill. But Foundayo isn't simply an injectable GLP-1 turned into a tablet. Wegovy is now available as an oral semaglutide tablet, giving patients another alternative to weekly GLP-1 injections. One of the most interesting developments is the science itself. Oral Wegovy contains the peptide semaglutide and uses a formulation designed to help it be absorbed orally. Foundayo takes a completely different approach: orforglipron is a small molecule rather than a peptide, but it targets the same GLP-1 receptor. payload.title: Launch HN: RonanRX (YC S26) – Personalized Peptides and GLP-1s
payload.summary: Hi HN, I’m Lloyd, one of two founders of RonanRx ( https://ronanrx.com/ ). We are building a vertically integrated pharmaceutical company with software for prescribing, telehealth, compounding, manufacturing, and delivery. We are starting with GLP-1s and peptides. The path to RonanRx is fairly unconventional. During the pandemic, I built one of the largest mask manufacturing factories in the US. We could make a million masks in a day. We converted raw polypropylene pellets into finished pallets of masks. I had a background in software from my YC W10 company, so we took a software approach to building our factory. payload.title: CJC-1295 Explained: Does It Really Increase Growth Hormone?
payload.summary: Does CJC-1295 really increase growth hormone? 🧬 CJC-1295 is often discussed alongside growth hormone, muscle growth, fat loss, recovery, and anti-aging—but CJC-1295 is not growth hormone. It's a synthetic analog of growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH) designed to stimulate the pituitary gland, which can increase the body's own release of growth hormone (GH) and raise IGF-1 levels. Early human research involving the long-acting DAC form of CJC-1295 found that a single dose produced sustained increases in average growth hormone and IGF-1 levels. But there's an important distinction: Increasing GH and IGF-1 does NOT automatically prove that CJC-1295 builds muscle, burns fat, improves longevity, or reverses aging. Changing a biomarker and demonstrating a meaningful clinical benefit are two very different things. In the study, participants first received weekly VK2735 and lost approximately 16% to 19% of their body weight after 21 weeks. Researchers then tested less-frequent maintenance dosing. The results were fascinating: 💉 Every-other-week dosing maintained up to 97% of previous weight loss 📅 Once-monthly dosing maintained up to 90% ⚖️ Participants switched to placebo maintained about 61% 📉 A small weekly-treatment group reached an average 21.7% weight loss after 33 weeks But there's an important distinction: this does not mean people started with a once-a-month injection and lost 20% of their body weight. Participants first lost weight using weekly VK2735. Researchers then tested whether less-frequent dosing could help maintain those results. That raises a much bigger question for the future of GLP-1 treatment: Could people eventually lose weight with weekly injections, then transition to one injection a month for maintenance? In this video, we break down how VK2735 works, GLP-1 + GIP signaling, the new maintenance data, side effects, limitations of the study, and why the next generation of obesity drugs may compete not only on how much weight people lose — but how rarely they need to take the medication. The path to RonanRx is fairly unconventional. During the pandemic, I built one of the largest mask manufacturing factories in the US. We could make a million masks in a day. We converted raw polypropylene pellets into finished pallets of masks. I had a background in software from my YC W10 company, so we took a software approach to building our factory. We used machine learning and computer vision to optimize production. We also vertically integrated almost everything. It worked. We built an efficient manufacturing operation and grew the business to 50 million dollars in revenue. Then people actually stopped caring about masks. Fair enough. But when someone loses 40 or 50 pounds, there's an important question most people aren't asking: How much of that weight was fat — and how much was lean mass? In this video, Peptide A to Z examines the growing concern around GLP-1 drugs and muscle loss. Research shows that people taking GLP-1 medications can lose measurable amounts of lean body mass along with fat. But the full story is more complicated than headlines suggesting these drugs simply “eat your muscle.” We break down: 💉 GLP-1 weight loss and lean mass 🔥 Fat loss vs. muscle loss 📊 What the STEP 1 semaglutide data actually showed 🫀 Why visceral fat matters 💪 Why preserving muscle becomes increasingly important with age 🧬 The new PROACT clinical trial 🔬 S-pindolol benzoate, also known as ACM-001.1 🏋️ Protein, resistance training and muscle preservation ⚖️ Why researchers are focusing on the quality of weight loss In the STEP 1 body-composition analysis, semaglutide was associated with approximately 19% lower total fat mass and 27% lower visceral fat, while lean body mass declined by about 10%. payload.title: GLP-1 Once a Month?! New VK2735 Results Could Change Weight Loss
payload.summary: What if you didn't have to take a GLP-1 every week — but only once a month? New clinical trial results for VK2735, an experimental GLP-1/GIP drug from Viking Therapeutics, suggest that less-frequent dosing could eventually play a role in maintaining weight loss. In the study, participants first received weekly VK2735 and lost approximately 16% to 19% of their body weight after 21 weeks. Researchers then tested less-frequent maintenance dosing. The results were fascinating: 💉 Every-other-week dosing maintained up to 97% of previous weight loss 📅 Once-monthly dosing maintained up to 90% ⚖️ Participants switched to placebo maintained about 61% 📉 A small weekly-treatment group reached an average 21.7% weight loss after 33 weeks But there's an important distinction: this does not mean people started with a once-a-month injection and lost 20% of their body weight. Participants first lost weight using weekly VK2735. Researchers then tested whether less-frequent dosing could help maintain those results. That raises a much bigger question for the future of GLP-1 treatment: Could people eventually lose weight with weekly injections, then transition to one injection a month for maintenance? In this video, we break down how VK2735 works, GLP-1 + GIP signaling, the new maintenance data, side effects, limitations of the study, and why the next generation of obesity drugs may compete not only on how much weight people lose — but how rarely they need to take the medication. payload.title: GLP-1 Pills Are Here — Are They Better Than the Shots?
payload.summary: GLP-1 weight-loss pills are officially here. But are they actually better than injections — or do they come with the same risks in a different package? You may have seen Martha Stewart advertising Foundayo, Lilly's new once-daily GLP-1 pill. But Foundayo isn't simply an injectable GLP-1 turned into a tablet. Its active ingredient, orforglipron, is a non-peptide small molecule designed to activate the GLP-1 receptor. And it's not the only option. Wegovy is now available as an oral semaglutide tablet, giving patients another alternative to weekly GLP-1 injections. In this video, Peptide A to Z breaks down: 💊 GLP-1 pills vs. injections 🧬 How oral Wegovy and Foundayo are different ⚖️ The potential advantages and disadvantages of GLP-1 pills 📉 What clinical trials show about weight loss 🍽️ Appetite control and delayed gastric emptying ⚠️ Side effects and important safety considerations 💉 Daily pills vs. weekly injections 🔬 Why orforglipron isn't actually a peptide 📺 What to know about the Martha Stewart Foundayo campaign 🤔 And the big question: Are GLP-1 pills actually better than the shots? One of the most interesting developments is the science itself. Oral Wegovy contains the peptide semaglutide and uses a formulation designed to help it be absorbed orally. Foundayo takes a completely different approach: orforglipron is a small molecule rather than a peptide, but it targets the same GLP-1 receptor. payload.title: BPC-157 Is EXPLODING — New Data Shows a 33X Surge
payload.summary: BPC-157 use appears to be exploding. New 2026 research found a 33-fold increase in newly documented BPC-157 users, rising from just 4 in the first quarter of 2020 to 134 in the first quarter of 2026 within a large medical-record network. But the most surprising number may be 79%. Among BPC-157 users whose medical records contained a clear outcome, about 79% had improvement documented. Does that mean BPC-157 actually works? Not so fast. In this video, Peptide A to Z breaks down the new BPC-157 research, including: • Where the 33X increase actually comes from • Why documented BPC-157 use is rising • What people are using BPC-157 for • The truth behind the reported 79% improvement rate • Why most improvements were patient-reported • BPC-157 and TB-500 — the “Wolverine Stack” • What the FDA says about BPC-157 • Why BPC-157 is still not FDA approved • What human evidence we actually have • What researchers still need to prove The new study examined clinical records from a network covering 15.2 million patients and identified 1,039 confirmed BPC-157 users. It's one of the most interesting looks yet at how this controversial peptide is being used in the real world. But there's an important distinction between popularity and proof. The study was observational, had no placebo group, did not use a standardized BPC-157 dose or treatment period, and many patients were using other therapies at the same time. The research was also released as a preprint and has not yet completed peer…

The path to RonanRx is fairly unconventional. During the pandemic, I built one of the largest mask manufacturing factories in the US. We could make a million masks in a day. We converted raw polypropylene pellets into finished pallets of masks. I had a background in software from my YC W10 company, so we took a software approach to building our factory. We used machine learning and computer vision to optimize production. We also vertically integrated almost everything. It worked. We built an efficient manufacturing operation and grew the business to 50 million dollars in revenue. Then people actually stopped caring about masks. Fair enough. payload.title: Your Relationship Shouldn't Be A Drag
payload.summary: Ep. 1012: Join us as we sit down with Margarita Nazarenko – globally recognised voice in feminine psychology, confidence, and identity. Margarita gets candid about anxious attachment, people-pleasing, relationship adrenaline, and the childhood patterns that can influence who we become in love. She shares the counterintuitive ways to handle conflict, boundaries, communication, and disrespect without chasing, or giving away your power. She also reveals the mindset shift that changed the way she approached relationships and ultimately helped her create the life and marriage she wanted.

payload.title: GLP-1 Once a Month?! New VK2735 Results Could Change Weight Loss
payload.summary: What if you didn't have to take a GLP-1 every week — but only once a month? New clinical trial results for VK2735, an experimental GLP-1/GIP drug from Viking Therapeutics, suggest that less-frequent dosing could eventually play a role in maintaining weight loss. In the study, participants first received weekly VK2735 and lost approximately 16% to 19% of their body weight after 21 weeks. Researchers then tested less-frequent maintenance dosing. The results were fascinating: 💉 Every-other-week dosing maintained up to 97% of previous weight loss 📅 Once-monthly dosing maintained up to 90% ⚖️ Participants switched to placebo maintained about 61% 📉 A small weekly-treatment group reached an average 21.7% weight loss after 33 weeks But there's an important distinction: this does not mean people started with a once-a-month injection and lost 20% of their body weight. Participants first lost weight using weekly VK2735. Researchers then tested whether less-frequent dosing could help maintain those results. That raises a much bigger question for the future of GLP-1 treatment: Could people eventually lose weight with weekly injections, then transition to one injection a month for maintenance? In this video, we break down how VK2735 works, GLP-1 + GIP signaling, the new maintenance data, side effects, limitations of the study, and why the next generation of obesity drugs may compete not only on how much weight people lose — but how rarely they need to take the medication. payload.title: Launch HN: RonanRX (YC S26) – Personalized Peptides and GLP-1s
payload.summary: Hi HN, I’m Lloyd, one of two founders of RonanRx ( https://ronanrx.com/ ). We are building a vertically integrated pharmaceutical company with software for prescribing, telehealth, compounding, manufacturing, and delivery. We are starting with GLP-1s and peptides. The path to RonanRx is fairly unconventional. During the pandemic, I built one of the largest mask manufacturing factories in the US. We could make a million masks in a day. We converted raw polypropylene pellets into finished pallets of masks. I had a background in software from my YC W10 company, so we took a software approach to building our factory. We used machine learning and computer vision to optimize production. We also vertically integrated almost everything. It worked. We built an efficient manufacturing operation and grew the business to 50 million dollars in revenue. Then people actually stopped caring about masks. Fair enough. payload.title: GLP-1 Once a Month?! New VK2735 Results Could Change Weight Loss

payload.title: Pilates Is Incredible For Birth
payload.summary: Ep. 1,011: Join Lauryn Bosstick as she sits down with Bryony Deery – Pilates instructor, entrepreneur, mother, author, and founder of Pilates by Bryony. They discuss preparing your body for pregnancy, postpartum wellness, the power of Pilates, and the importance of protecting your time, privacy, and energy in an always-on world. Bryony shares how she stays disciplined while balancing motherhood and business, and why creating boundaries with social media leads to more presence and connection. Plus, Bryony breaks down how she turned her passion for Pilates into a business, why staying niche matters, and how she built a community that continues to grow with her.

payload.title: GLP-1s Are Melting Fat — But What About Your MUSCLE?
payload.summary: GLP-1 drugs like Wegovy and Zepbound can produce dramatic weight loss. But when someone loses 40 or 50 pounds, there's an important question most people aren't asking: How much of that weight was fat — and how much was lean mass? In this video, Peptide A to Z examines the growing concern around GLP-1 drugs and muscle loss. Research shows that people taking GLP-1 medications can lose measurable amounts of lean body mass along with fat. But the full story is more complicated than headlines suggesting these drugs simply “eat your muscle.” We break down: 💉 GLP-1 weight loss and lean mass 🔥 Fat loss vs. muscle loss 📊 What the STEP 1 semaglutide data actually showed 🫀 Why visceral fat matters 💪 Why preserving muscle becomes increasingly important with age 🧬 The new PROACT clinical trial 🔬 S-pindolol benzoate, also known as ACM-001.1 🏋️ Protein, resistance training and muscle preservation ⚖️ Why researchers are focusing on the quality of weight loss In the STEP 1 body-composition analysis, semaglutide was associated with approximately 19% lower total fat mass and 27% lower visceral fat, while lean body mass declined by about 10%. So yes, lean mass can decrease. But substantially more fat was lost, meaning overall body composition improved. Now researchers want to know whether they can do even better. payload.title: GLP-1 Once a Month?! New VK2735 Results Could Change Weight Loss
payload.summary: What if you didn't have to take a GLP-1 every week — but only once a month? New clinical trial results for VK2735, an experimental GLP-1/GIP drug from Viking Therapeutics, suggest that less-frequent dosing could eventually play a role in maintaining weight loss. In the study, participants first received weekly VK2735 and lost approximately 16% to 19% of their body weight after 21 weeks. Researchers then tested less-frequent maintenance dosing. The results were fascinating: 💉 Every-other-week dosing maintained up to 97% of previous weight loss 📅 Once-monthly dosing maintained up to 90% ⚖️ Participants switched to placebo maintained about 61% 📉 A small weekly-treatment group reached an average 21.7% weight loss after 33 weeks But there's an important distinction: this does not mean people started with a once-a-month injection and lost 20% of their body weight. Participants first lost weight using weekly VK2735. Researchers then tested whether less-frequent dosing could help maintain those results. That raises a much bigger question for the future of GLP-1 treatment: Could people eventually lose weight with weekly injections, then transition to one injection a month for maintenance? In this video, we break down how VK2735 works, GLP-1 + GIP signaling, the new maintenance data, side effects, limitations of the study, and why the next generation of obesity drugs may compete not only on how much weight people lose — but how rarely they need to take the medication. payload.title: GLP-1 Pills Are Here — Are They Better Than the Shots?
payload.summary: GLP-1 weight-loss pills are officially here. But are they actually better than injections — or do they come with the same risks in a different package? You may have seen Martha Stewart advertising Foundayo, Lilly's new once-daily GLP-1 pill. But Foundayo isn't simply an injectable GLP-1 turned into a tablet. Its active ingredient, orforglipron, is a non-peptide small molecule designed to activate the GLP-1 receptor. And it's not the only option. Wegovy is now available as an oral semaglutide tablet, giving patients another alternative to weekly GLP-1 injections. In this video, Peptide A to Z breaks down: 💊 GLP-1 pills vs. injections 🧬 How oral Wegovy and Foundayo are different ⚖️ The potential advantages and disadvantages of GLP-1 pills 📉 What clinical trials show about weight loss 🍽️ Appetite control and delayed gastric emptying ⚠️ Side effects and important safety considerations 💉 Daily pills vs. weekly injections 🔬 Why orforglipron isn't actually a peptide 📺 What to know about the Martha Stewart Foundayo campaign 🤔 And the big question: Are GLP-1 pills actually better than the shots? One of the most interesting developments is the science itself. Oral Wegovy contains the peptide semaglutide and uses a formulation designed to help it be absorbed orally. Foundayo takes a completely different approach: orforglipron is a small molecule rather than a peptide, but it targets the same GLP-1 receptor. payload.title: BPC-157 Is EXPLODING — New Data Shows a 33X Surge
payload.summary: BPC-157 use appears to be exploding. New 2026 research found a 33-fold increase in newly documented BPC-157 users, rising from just 4 in the first quarter of 2020 to 134 in the first quarter of 2026 within a large medical-record network. But the most surprising number may be 79%. Among BPC-157 users whose medical records contained a clear outcome, about 79% had improvement documented. Does that mean BPC-157 actually works? Not so fast. In this video, Peptide A to Z breaks down the new BPC-157 research, including: • Where the 33X increase actually comes from • Why documented BPC-157 use is rising • What people are using BPC-157 for • The truth behind the reported 79% improvement rate • Why most improvements were patient-reported • BPC-157 and TB-500 — the “Wolverine Stack” • What the FDA says about BPC-157 • Why BPC-157 is still not FDA approved • What human evidence we actually have • What researchers still need to prove The new study examined clinical records from a network covering 15.2 million patients and identified 1,039 confirmed BPC-157 users. It's one of the most interesting looks yet at how this controversial peptide is being used in the real world. But there's an important distinction between popularity and proof. The study was observational, had no placebo group, did not use a standardized BPC-157 dose or treatment period, and many patients were using other therapies at the same time. The research was also released as a preprint and has not yet completed peer…

payload.summary: Hi HN, I’m Lloyd, one of two founders of RonanRx ( https://ronanrx.com/ ). We are building a vertically integrated pharmaceutical company with software for prescribing, telehealth, compounding, manufacturing, and delivery. We are starting with GLP-1s and peptides. The path to RonanRx is fairly unconventional. During the pandemic, I built one of the largest mask manufacturing factories in the US. We could make a million masks in a day. We converted raw polypropylene pellets into finished pallets of masks. I had a background in software from my YC W10 company, so we took a software approach to building our factory. We used machine learning and computer vision to optimize production. We also vertically integrated almost everything. It worked. We built an efficient manufacturing operation and grew the business to 50 million dollars in revenue. Then people actually stopped caring about masks. Fair enough. Around the same time, I decided to try and lose the weight I had gained while building the factory. I ate nothing but chicken for six months. While this diet got some results, I plateaued. My doctor suggested tirzepatide, a GLP-1 medication. For me, losing weight was only the beginning. "Food noise" was gone. I showed less interest in other compulsive behavior. I stopped scrolling Instagram and quit biting my nails. But that was just the beginning. I was born with a congenital heart defect called aortic stenosis. payload.title: Not Every Biohack Is Worth Trying
payload.summary: 🚫 Not Every Biohack Deserves a Try When Dr. Kevin White was asked about biohacks that seem crazy or need more research, he had a very clear example: drinking urine. He shared that he had heard of patients practicing urine drinking and questioned the reasoning behind it. His response was simple: just because something is labeled a “biohack” doesn’t mean it should automatically be considered a wellness strategy. The path to RonanRx is fairly unconventional. During the pandemic, I built one of the largest mask manufacturing factories in the US. We could make a million masks in a day. We converted raw polypropylene pellets into finished pallets of masks. I had a background in software from my YC W10 company, so we took a software approach to building our factory. We used machine learning and computer vision to optimize production. We also vertically integrated almost everything. It worked. We built an efficient manufacturing operation and grew the business to 50 million dollars in revenue. Then people actually stopped caring about masks. Fair enough. Around the same time, I decided to try and lose the weight I had gained while building the factory. I ate nothing but chicken for six months. While this diet got some results, I plateaued. payload.title: GLP-1 Once a Month?! New VK2735 Results Could Change Weight Loss
payload.summary: What if you didn't have to take a GLP-1 every week — but only once a month? New clinical trial results for VK2735, an experimental GLP-1/GIP drug from Viking Therapeutics, suggest that less-frequent dosing could eventually play a role in maintaining weight loss. In the study, participants first received weekly VK2735 and lost approximately 16% to 19% of their body weight after 21 weeks. Researchers then tested less-frequent maintenance dosing. The results were fascinating: 💉 Every-other-week dosing maintained up to 97% of previous weight loss 📅 Once-monthly dosing maintained up to 90% ⚖️ Participants switched to placebo maintained about 61% 📉 A small weekly-treatment group reached an average 21.7% weight loss after 33 weeks But there's an important distinction: this does not mean people started with a once-a-month injection and lost 20% of their body weight. Participants first lost weight using weekly VK2735. Researchers then tested whether less-frequent dosing could help maintain those results. That raises a much bigger question for the future of GLP-1 treatment: Could people eventually lose weight with weekly injections, then transition to one injection a month for maintenance? In this video, we break down how VK2735 works, GLP-1 + GIP signaling, the new maintenance data, side effects, limitations of the study, and why the next generation of obesity drugs may compete not only on how much weight people lose — but how rarely they need to take the medication. payload.title: BPC-157 Is EXPLODING — New Data Shows a 33X Surge
payload.summary: BPC-157 use appears to be exploding. New 2026 research found a 33-fold increase in newly documented BPC-157 users, rising from just 4 in the first quarter of 2020 to 134 in the first quarter of 2026 within a large medical-record network. But the most surprising number may be 79%. Among BPC-157 users whose medical records contained a clear outcome, about 79% had improvement documented. Does that mean BPC-157 actually works? Not so fast. In this video, Peptide A to Z breaks down the new BPC-157 research, including: • Where the 33X increase actually comes from • Why documented BPC-157 use is rising • What people are using BPC-157 for • The truth behind the reported 79% improvement rate • Why most improvements were patient-reported • BPC-157 and TB-500 — the “Wolverine Stack” • What the FDA says about BPC-157 • Why BPC-157 is still not FDA approved • What human evidence we actually have • What researchers still need to prove The new study examined clinical records from a network covering 15.2 million patients and identified 1,039 confirmed BPC-157 users. It's one of the most interesting looks yet at how this controversial peptide is being used in the real world. But there's an important distinction between popularity and proof. The study was observational, had no placebo group, did not use a standardized BPC-157 dose or treatment period, and many patients were using other therapies at the same time. The research was also released as a preprint and has not yet completed peer…

Research shows that people taking GLP-1 medications can lose measurable amounts of lean body mass along with fat. payload.title: GLP-1 Once a Month?! New VK2735 Results Could Change Weight Loss
payload.summary: What if you didn't have to take a GLP-1 every week — but only once a month? New clinical trial results for VK2735, an experimental GLP-1/GIP drug from Viking Therapeutics, suggest that less-frequent dosing could eventually play a role in maintaining weight loss. In the study, participants first received weekly VK2735 and lost approximately 16% to 19% of their body weight after 21 weeks. Researchers then tested less-frequent maintenance dosing. The results were fascinating: 💉 Every-other-week dosing maintained up to 97% of previous weight loss 📅 Once-monthly dosing maintained up to 90% ⚖️ Participants switched to placebo maintained about 61% 📉 A small weekly-treatment group reached an average 21.7% weight loss after 33 weeks But there's an important distinction: this does not mean people started with a once-a-month injection and lost 20% of their body weight. Participants first lost weight using weekly VK2735. Researchers then tested whether less-frequent dosing could help maintain those results. That raises a much bigger question for the future of GLP-1 treatment: Could people eventually lose weight with weekly injections, then transition to one injection a month for maintenance? In this video, we break down how VK2735 works, GLP-1 + GIP signaling, the new maintenance data, side effects, limitations of the study, and why the next generation of obesity drugs may compete not only on how much weight people lose — but how rarely they need to take the medication. payload.title: GLP-1 Pills Are Here — Are They Better Than the Shots?
payload.summary: GLP-1 weight-loss pills are officially here. But are they actually better than injections — or do they come with the same risks in a different package? You may have seen Martha Stewart advertising Foundayo, Lilly's new once-daily GLP-1 pill. But Foundayo isn't simply an injectable GLP-1 turned into a tablet. Its active ingredient, orforglipron, is a non-peptide small molecule designed to activate the GLP-1 receptor. And it's not the only option. Wegovy is now available as an oral semaglutide tablet, giving patients another alternative to weekly GLP-1 injections. In this video, Peptide A to Z breaks down: 💊 GLP-1 pills vs. injections 🧬 How oral Wegovy and Foundayo are different ⚖️ The potential advantages and disadvantages of GLP-1 pills 📉 What clinical trials show about weight loss 🍽️ Appetite control and delayed gastric emptying ⚠️ Side effects and important safety considerations 💉 Daily pills vs. weekly injections 🔬 Why orforglipron isn't actually a peptide 📺 What to know about the Martha Stewart Foundayo campaign 🤔 And the big question: Are GLP-1 pills actually better than the shots? One of the most interesting developments is the science itself. Oral Wegovy contains the peptide semaglutide and uses a formulation designed to help it be absorbed orally. Foundayo takes a completely different approach: orforglipron is a small molecule rather than a peptide, but it targets the same GLP-1 receptor. payload.title: BPC-157 Is EXPLODING — New Data Shows a 33X Surge
payload.summary: BPC-157 use appears to be exploding. New 2026 research found a 33-fold increase in newly documented BPC-157 users, rising from just 4 in the first quarter of 2020 to 134 in the first quarter of 2026 within a large medical-record network. But the most surprising number may be 79%. Among BPC-157 users whose medical records contained a clear outcome, about 79% had improvement documented. Does that mean BPC-157 actually works? Not so fast. In this video, Peptide A to Z breaks down the new BPC-157 research, including: • Where the 33X increase actually comes from • Why documented BPC-157 use is rising • What people are using BPC-157 for • The truth behind the reported 79% improvement rate • Why most improvements were patient-reported • BPC-157 and TB-500 — the “Wolverine Stack” • What the FDA says about BPC-157 • Why BPC-157 is still not FDA approved • What human evidence we actually have • What researchers still need to prove The new study examined clinical records from a network covering 15.2 million patients and identified 1,039 confirmed BPC-157 users. It's one of the most interesting looks yet at how this controversial peptide is being used in the real world. But there's an important distinction between popularity and proof. The study was observational, had no placebo group, did not use a standardized BPC-157 dose or treatment period, and many patients were using other therapies at the same time. The research was also released as a preprint and has not yet completed peer…

We converted raw polypropylene pellets into finished pallets of masks. I had a background in software from my YC W10 company, so we took a software approach to building our factory. We used machine learning and computer vision to optimize production. We also vertically integrated almost everything. It worked. payload.title: GLP-1 Once a Month?! New VK2735 Results Could Change Weight Loss
payload.summary: What if you didn't have to take a GLP-1 every week — but only once a month? New clinical trial results for VK2735, an experimental GLP-1/GIP drug from Viking Therapeutics, suggest that less-frequent dosing could eventually play a role in maintaining weight loss. In the study, participants first received weekly VK2735 and lost approximately 16% to 19% of their body weight after 21 weeks. Researchers then tested less-frequent maintenance dosing. The results were fascinating: 💉 Every-other-week dosing maintained up to 97% of previous weight loss 📅 Once-monthly dosing maintained up to 90% ⚖️ Participants switched to placebo maintained about 61% 📉 A small weekly-treatment group reached an average 21.7% weight loss after 33 weeks But there's an important distinction: this does not mean people started with a once-a-month injection and lost 20% of their body weight. Participants first lost weight using weekly VK2735. Researchers then tested whether less-frequent dosing could help maintain those results. That raises a much bigger question for the future of GLP-1 treatment: Could people eventually lose weight with weekly injections, then transition to one injection a month for maintenance? In this video, we break down how VK2735 works, GLP-1 + GIP signaling, the new maintenance data, side effects, limitations of the study, and why the next generation of obesity drugs may compete not only on how much weight people lose — but how rarely they need to take the medication. payload.title: BPC-157 Is EXPLODING — New Data Shows a 33X Surge
payload.summary: BPC-157 use appears to be exploding. New 2026 research found a 33-fold increase in newly documented BPC-157 users, rising from just 4 in the first quarter of 2020 to 134 in the first quarter of 2026 within a large medical-record network. But the most surprising number may be 79%. Among BPC-157 users whose medical records contained a clear outcome, about 79% had improvement documented. Does that mean BPC-157 actually works? Not so fast. In this video, Peptide A to Z breaks down the new BPC-157 research, including: • Where the 33X increase actually comes from • Why documented BPC-157 use is rising • What people are using BPC-157 for • The truth behind the reported 79% improvement rate • Why most improvements were patient-reported • BPC-157 and TB-500 — the “Wolverine Stack” • What the FDA says about BPC-157 • Why BPC-157 is still not FDA approved • What human evidence we actually have • What researchers still need to prove The new study examined clinical records from a network covering 15.2 million patients and identified 1,039 confirmed BPC-157 users. It's one of the most interesting looks yet at how this controversial peptide is being used in the real world. But there's an important distinction between popularity and proof. The study was observational, had no placebo group, did not use a standardized BPC-157 dose or treatment period, and many patients were using other therapies at the same time. The research was also released as a preprint and has not yet completed peer…

payload.title: Orexin Explained: The Peptide That Keeps Your Brain Awake
payload.summary: What if one tiny peptide system in your brain helps determine whether you stay awake or fall asleep? In this episode of Peptide A to Z, we break down orexin, a naturally occurring peptide system that plays a major role in wakefulness, alertness, sleep, and narcolepsy. People with narcolepsy type 1 lose most of the brain cells that produce orexin. Without enough orexin signaling, the brain can struggle to maintain the normal boundary between being awake and asleep—leading to severe daytime sleepiness, cataplexy, sleep paralysis, and other symptoms. But in 2026, the orexin story reached a major milestone. We explore how researchers developed a new approach that targets the orexin 2 receptor, why this is fundamentally different from simply using a stimulant, and how the same peptide system can actually be targeted in the opposite direction to help treat insomnia. In this video: • What orexin A and orexin B are • How orexin helps keep the brain awake • The connection between orexin and narcolepsy type 1 • What cataplexy is • The 2026 breakthrough in orexin-targeted treatment • Why blocking orexin can help people sleep • Orexin's potential roles in appetite, motivation, reward, stress, and metabolism • Why this peptide system could become increasingly important in medicine One peptide system. Turn it down to help people sleep. Turn it up to help people stay awake. Subscribe to Peptide A to Z for straightforward breakdowns of peptide research, clinical studies, and emerging…

payload.title: How to Workout Your TONGUE!?

After years of helping people pursue beauty through injections and cosmetic procedures, Shelly began noticing their limitations and that these methods didn't truly solve what people were seeking. Today, Shelly teaches a functional approach to beauty that focuses on restoring facial health, structure, and vitality from the inside out. In this episode, Shelly gets real about facial manipulation, facial exercise, lymphatic drainage, fascia release, and the connection between muscle, bone, and skin as we age. She breaks down how tongue posture, nasal breathing, chewing, posture, and modern habits can impact jawline and facial structure, plus her approach to mouth taping, mewing, myofunctional therapy, and daily facial rituals. Shelly also shares her perspective as a former injector on fillers and injectables, why foundational practices matter, and how to build a more natural, intentional approach to aging well.

payload.title: How to Rebuild Your Life After Addiction, Relapse & Rock Bottom

After nearly a decade sober, Juliet relapsed – despite having built what outwardly looked like a stable, successful life. She got sober again at 38 and began rebuilding from the inside out, focusing on accountability, spiritual discipline, and daily structure. In this episode, Juliet gets candid about the realities of addiction and what it takes to maintain sobriety through different seasons of life. She shares practical lessons on recognizing triggers, creating structure, asking for help, taking accountability, and navigating relapse without letting it define you. She also opens up about the role of faith, family, motherhood, and community in her recovery – and how to build a life that supports long-term sobriety. Most importantly, Juliet shares why recovery isn’t about perfection, but about continuing to choose yourself and get back up. Without enough orexin signaling, the brain can struggle to maintain the normal boundary between being awake and asleep—leading to severe daytime sleepiness, cataplexy, sleep paralysis, and other symptoms. But in 2026, the orexin story reached a major milestone. We explore how researchers developed a new approach that targets the orexin 2 receptor, why this is fundamentally different from simply using a stimulant, and how the same peptide system can actually be targeted in the opposite direction to help treat insomnia. payload.title: Chewing Can Help Sculpt Your Face!
payload.summary: Ep. 1,009: Join us as we sit down with Shelly Marshall – also known as Beauty Shamans is an esthetician, former nurse injector, and founder of Beauty Shamans Skincare and the Skin Within Studio. After years of helping people pursue beauty through injections and cosmetic procedures, Shelly began noticing their limitations and that these methods didn't truly solve what people were seeking. Today, Shelly teaches a functional approach to beauty that focuses on restoring facial health, structure, and vitality from the inside out. In this episode, Shelly gets real about facial manipulation, facial exercise, lymphatic drainage, fascia release, and the connection between muscle, bone, and skin as we age. She breaks down how tongue posture, nasal breathing, chewing, posture, and modern habits can impact jawline and facial structure, plus her approach to mouth taping, mewing, myofunctional therapy, and daily facial rituals. Shelly also shares her perspective as a former injector on fillers and injectables, why foundational practices matter, and how to build a more natural, intentional approach to aging well.

payload.title: GLP-1 Once a Month?! New VK2735 Results Could Change Weight Loss
payload.summary: What if you didn't have to take a GLP-1 every week — but only once a month? New clinical trial results for VK2735, an experimental GLP-1/GIP drug from Viking Therapeutics, suggest that less-frequent dosing could eventually play a role in maintaining weight loss. In the study, participants first received weekly VK2735 and lost approximately 16% to 19% of their body weight after 21 weeks. Researchers then tested less-frequent maintenance dosing. The results were fascinating: 💉 Every-other-week dosing maintained up to 97% of previous weight loss 📅 Once-monthly dosing maintained up to 90% ⚖️ Participants switched to placebo maintained about 61% 📉 A small weekly-treatment group reached an average 21.7% weight loss after 33 weeks But there's an important distinction: this does not mean people started with a once-a-month injection and lost 20% of their body weight. Participants first lost weight using weekly VK2735. Researchers then tested whether less-frequent dosing could help maintain those results. That raises a much bigger question for the future of GLP-1 treatment: Could people eventually lose weight with weekly injections, then transition to one injection a month for maintenance? payload.title: Orexin Explained: The Peptide That Keeps Your Brain Awake
payload.summary: What if one tiny peptide system in your brain helps determine whether you stay awake or fall asleep? In this episode of Peptide A to Z, we break down orexin, a naturally occurring peptide system that plays a major role in wakefulness, alertness, sleep, and narcolepsy. People with narcolepsy type 1 lose most of the brain cells that produce orexin. Without enough orexin signaling, the brain can struggle to maintain the normal boundary between being awake and asleep—leading to severe daytime sleepiness, cataplexy, sleep paralysis, and other symptoms. But in 2026, the orexin story reached a major milestone. We explore how researchers developed a new approach that targets the orexin 2 receptor, why this is fundamentally different from simply using a stimulant, and how the same peptide system can actually be targeted in the opposite direction to help treat insomnia. In this video: • What orexin A and orexin B are • How orexin helps keep the brain awake • The connection between orexin and narcolepsy type 1 • What cataplexy is • The 2026 breakthrough in orexin-targeted treatment • Why blocking orexin can help people sleep • Orexin's potential roles in appetite, motivation, reward, stress, and metabolism • Why this peptide system could become increasingly important in medicine One peptide system. Turn it down to help people sleep. Turn it up to help people stay awake. Subscribe to Peptide A to Z for straightforward breakdowns of peptide research, clinical studies, and emerging…

payload.title: Chewing Can Help Sculpt Your Face!
payload.summary: Ep. 1,009: Join us as we sit down with Shelly Marshall – also known as Beauty Shamans is an esthetician, former nurse injector, and founder of Beauty Shamans Skincare and the Skin Within Studio. After years of helping people pursue beauty through injections and cosmetic procedures, Shelly began noticing their limitations and that these methods didn't truly solve what people were seeking. Today, Shelly teaches a functional approach to beauty that focuses on restoring facial health, structure, and vitality from the inside out. In this episode, Shelly gets real about facial manipulation, facial exercise, lymphatic drainage, fascia release, and the connection between muscle, bone, and skin as we age. She breaks down how tongue posture, nasal breathing, chewing, posture, and modern habits can impact jawline and facial structure, plus her approach to mouth taping, mewing, myofunctional therapy, and daily facial rituals. Shelly also shares her perspective as a former injector on fillers and injectables, why foundational practices matter, and how to build a more natural, intentional approach to aging well.

You may have seen Martha Stewart advertising Foundayo, Lilly's new once-daily GLP-1 pill. But Foundayo isn't simply an injectable GLP-1 turned into a tablet. Its active ingredient, orforglipron, is a non-peptide small molecule designed to activate the GLP-1 receptor. And it's not the only option. Wegovy is now available as an oral semaglutide tablet, giving patients another alternative to weekly GLP-1 injections.
